description:
We are Computer Science students interested in software development, space exploration, and innovative technology. We aim to build an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that makes lunar and Martian missions engaging through simulation, resource management, and decision-making.

We welcome collaborators interested in programming, game development, UI/UX design, and space science who are eager to share ideas and build something meaningful together.
summary:
**Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: Junior Astronaut Academy**

Junior Astronaut Academy is an interactive, browser-based educational game developed to introduce students to the challenges of space exploration and operating an outpost beyond Earth. The project provides a mission-based environment where users can explore, interact with mission elements, and engage with activities through actions such as collecting, scanning, and running missions. It addresses the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by turning space-related learning into an interactive experience rather than relying only on traditional educational material. The project is important because it encourages curiosity about astronaut activities, lunar and Martian exploration, and STEM fields while making space education more engaging and accessible to younger learners.
details:
Project Details

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer: Junior Astronaut Academy is a browser-based interactive educational game developed to make space exploration more engaging and accessible to younger students.

The application provides an interactive mission environment where users can explore and interact with different mission elements through activities such as collecting, scanning, and running missions. These interactions introduce users to the idea of performing tasks in a space mission environment and encourage exploration through hands-on digital experiences.

Our project addresses the NASA Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge by transforming space-related learning into an interactive experience. Instead of simply reading about astronauts and space exploration, students can engage with a digital environment and explore mission activities themselves.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Vite. We used Visual Studio Code for development, GitHub for version control and collaboration, and Vercel to deploy the application. NASA's open API resources were used as a source of space-related information to support the educational context of the project.

Our creative approach focuses on combining game-based interaction with STEM education. We considered accessibility through a web-based format, ease of use for younger learners, and the importance of making space concepts understandable and engaging.

The intended impact is to encourage curiosity about astronaut activities, lunar and Martian exploration, and science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). The project was developed collaboratively by our two-member team.
